public_rationale: The 89% number has an identifiable counterpart in reporting about 34 AI startups. That measure is annualised, excludes public companies and AI cloud startups, and carries revenue-sharing caveats. It cannot establish the broader claim about the industry's realized annual revenue. The search did not establish a comparable total that proves or disproves the $20 billion ceiling.
limitations: Accessible coverage is secondary reporting of the underlying survey.
The reporting period, company universe, and accounting basis remain ambiguous.
An unknown accounting basis precludes a supported or contradicted financial grade.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: OpenAI and Anthropic represent 89% of the largest AI companies' revenues; excluding them, the AI industry makes at most $20B a year.

statement.excerpt: They want you to assume that all this money can’t be wrong, even though when you remove OpenAI and Anthropic (who represent 89% of the revenues of the largest AI companies) the AI industry is, at best, pulling in $20 billion in annual revenue.

from_speaker: 89% of the revenues of the largest AI companies
when you remove OpenAI and Anthropic
our_interpretation: The contextual industry is suppliers of generative AI models and applications. The speaker does not supply a company roster or clearly exclude public companies and infrastructure providers.
Annual revenue ordinarily means realized revenue over twelve months, rather than annualising a recent month.

For the ongoing annual revenue assertion, I use the trailing twelve months ending March 31, 2026: the latest routinely reported quarter-end available before the July 7 post. This reporting-window choice is mine.
The 89% assertion requires a defined largest-company cohort. The $20 billion ceiling applies to the remainder of the industry, not merely the remainder of that cohort.
Excluding the two companies is a calculation rule, not a conditional forecast.
The supplied words do not identify an accounting basis. Finding a similar press statistic does not establish that the entire assertion uses that statistic's basis.
criteria.support_condition: A consistent company roster and comparable realized annual revenues establish an approximately 89% share for OpenAI and Anthropic among the largest companies, and comprehensive industry coverage establishes no more than $20 billion for everyone else.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable realized annual revenue evidence shows that the two companies' share is materially different from 89%, or establishes more than $20 billion in revenue for the remaining industry. A sample, run rate, or different accounting basis is insufficient.
